headline: Held off on ordinance changes and moved next meeting earlier; discussed cable renegotiation and Public Access building cleanup.
summary: Members discussed renegotiating the cable franchise agreement to seek HD channels and other changes. Staff plan to clear out the Public Access building, and a request for bids for remediation work was issued. Members approved the prior meeting's minutes and held off on changing the ordinance.
decisions: Approved the September 3, 2026 meeting minutes unanimously.

Set the next meeting for a 3:30 PM start instead of 4 PM.

plain_text:
October 5, 2026 Cable TV Committee Meeting Minutes 
Present: Kathy, Lou, Pat, Jim, Danica, 2 members of the public in person, 1 member of the 
public online 
Excused: Richard 
Absent: John 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order at 4:01 p.m. 
The Chair of the Committee was excused from the meeting.  
Motion by Lou, seconded by Jim, to have Councilor Boston chair the meeting. 
Vote: Unanimous 
 
2. Adjustment(s) to Agenda 
There are no adjustments to the agenda. 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
3.a. September 3, 2026 Meeting Minutes 
Motion by Kathy, seconded by Lou, to approve the September 3, 2026 meeting 
minutes. 
 Vote: Unanimous 
 
4. New Business 
4.a. Ordinance Review 
Danica reviewed the Committee’s authority under Section 403 of the “Cable 
Television Committee; Public, Education and Governmental Access” ordinance.  
The Committee discussed the cable franchise agreement and the potential need for 
negotiation. Barry explained that the cable company’s current position is that any
changes to status quo that we would want to pursue, such as HD programming, 
requesting a lower channel number, or getting back the third channel, would require 
renegotiation.  
The Committee determined that before getting into a conversation about 
renegotiation, there would need to be work done to prepare, including lining up 
specialized legal representation and identifying what items are a priority for us to 
ask for in negotiations. In addition to HD channels and a third channel, members 
expressed interest in asking for help with reestablishing the six origination sites 
outlined in the existing agreement as well as potentially new equipment. 
It was noted that when the existing agreement was set to expire in 2020, it was 
determined to be in the City’s best interest to continue operating under an expired 
agreement rather than renegotiate. 
Pat asked what is in it for the cable company to give us beneficial terms in a 
renegotiation. Barry suggested that positive improvements to our channels put us in 
a better position to promote to people that they should watch on cable, which 
ultimately encourages additional subscribers. 
Jim asked if the ordinance should be brought forward to the Policy Committee for 
some minor housekeeping changes, such as the reference to a job title that no 
longer exists. Danica noted that once an ordinance is in the hands of a Committee 
or the Council, motions can be made to change anything in it. Jim said that we have 
the benefit of Councilor Boston as a strong advocate for our work. Lou expressed 
concerns about a review leading to decreased power for the Committee. Danica 
mentioned that at the last meeting, John had wanted to propose a new name for the 
Committee, which would also require an ordinance change. The members present 
opted to hold off on changes for now. 
 
4.b. Building Update 
Danica and Barry shared information about the status of the Public Access building. 
Two pest control companies have now been in the building and shared insight. 
Because of the extent of the mouse activity in the building, the companies have 
suggested that any porous surfaces should be considered contaminated with 
mouse urine or droppings and either need to be remediated or removed. Given the 
age and condition of the furniture items in the building, staff decided the most 
practical option was to get a dumpster and clear the space out. Jim has helped with 
cleanup tasks inside and out of the building.
Danica issued an RFB on Thursday for remediation work at the building. There is a 
walkthrough for interested bidders next week and bids are due by the end of the 
month.  
Thus far, the direction from the Interim City Manager has been that Danica will bring 
forward bids with a request to have this work paid for out of contingency funds. Jim 
noted that the expenditure of contingency funds requires a 2/3 majority approval of 
the Council. 
Jim emphasized that some of the external issues that he saw when he was 
volunteering are outside the scope of the remediation process, such as rotten wood 
around the windows, but should be addressed soon. 
 
5. Other Business 
Barry suggested that for a future agenda, the Committee should consider having a specific 
discussion about what would go on channels 3 and 85 and making a formal 
recommendation that he would follow. 
Barry has begun the process of setting up a YouTube channel for public access produced 
media. He also has an idea to take three of our best classic cameras and retrofit them to 
record digitally and will be researching this idea. 
Jim suggested there should be a formal inventory of equipment and record of what we own 
and maintain, including information such as serial numbers, life expectancy for the gear 
and other details to keep track of assets and help with budgeting for replacements. 
Barry shared that the Sustainability Commission is discussing building energy audits 
today, with the Public Access building specifically on the list to talk about. 
The Committee decided to schedule the next meeting for a 3:30 PM start time instead of 4 
PM. The members agreed to aim to keep the meeting to one hour, which would allow the 
use of the conference room instead of the Council Chambers. 
 
6. Adjourn 
Motion by Kathy, seconded by Lou, to adjourn the meeting. 
Meeting adjourned at 5:06 p.m.
